chapter_name: Chapter 05: Adjectives and Degrees of Comparison
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will deepen their understanding of adjectives, explore the correct order of multiple adjectives, and master advanced rules for degrees of comparison.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 A sentence without adjectives is like a black-and-white movie! But when we have multiple describing words, which one goes first? Is it a 'big red balloon' or a 'red big balloon'? Let's fine-tune our describing skills and learn the ultimate rules of comparison.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: We know adjectives describe nouns, but they fall into specific categories: Quality (what kind?), Quantity (how much for uncountable), Number (how many for countable), and Demonstrative (pointing out specific things: this, that, these, those).

lesson_modules.module_title: 📏 The Order of Adjectives (विशेषणों का सही क्रम)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: When using multiple adjectives before a noun, they must follow a specific order. A simple rule to remember is: Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Color, Origin, Material. (OSASCOM)

lesson_modules.module_title: ⚖️ Advanced Degrees of Comparison (तुलना के उन्नत नियम)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Beyond adding -er and -est, some rules are tricky. For example, never use a double comparative (like 'more smarter'). Also, when comparing one thing against all others in its group using the comparative degree, we use 'than any other'.
examples_or_templates: Wrong: He is more taller than me. -> Right: He is **taller** than me.
Rule: Iron is **more useful than any other** metal.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which sentence shows the correct order of adjectives?
❓ What kind of adjective is the word 'Much' in the phrase 'Much patience'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fix the grammatical error in this sentence: 'This puzzle is more easier than the last one.'
subjective_practice.hint: You have a double comparative! 'Easier' already means 'more easy'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rearrange these adjectives in the correct order: (leather / stylish / black) jacket.
subjective_practice.hint: Opinion comes first, then Color, then Material.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with the superlative degree of 'Bad'. 'That was the ____ movie I have ever seen.'
subjective_practice.hint: It is an irregular adjective. (Bad -> Worse -> ?)

activity_or_assignment.title: 🛍️ The Ultimate Sales Pitch
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Pick an ordinary object in your house (like a mug or a shoe). Write a 3-sentence 'sales pitch' to sell it to someone, using at least 5 different adjectives. Make sure you put them in the correct OSASCOM order!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Adjectives are categorized into Quality, Quantity, Number, and Demonstrative.
⭐ Multiple adjectives follow a specific sequence: Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Color, Origin, Material.
⭐ Never use double comparatives or superlatives (e.g., do not say 'most happiest').
